title: Climate-control materials, capacities and clutch gap
introduction:
I use this page to answer three different questions: which material is specified, which capacity applies to the engine, and which compressor-clutch clearance range belongs to that engine. Check the engine designation again in each table—the capacity groups and clutch-gap groups are arranged differently.

Think of this as the A/C system's recipe card: the ingredients and quantities matter, but they do not teach the cooking. These tables provide specifications, not refrigerant recovery and charging, compressor-oil replenishment, or clutch-gap measurement and adjustment procedures. Refrigerant service requires the correct recovery and charging equipment and the matching service procedure.

edits.text: Specified lubricants, fluids, sealers and adhesives
edits.why: Match the material description to its specification in the same row. The refrigerant entry includes market-specific product identifiers for the US, Canada and Mexico. A dash in the specification column leaves that field unspecified; it does not make the material interchangeable with any similarly named product.

I choose the engine group separately under the compressor-oil entry and the refrigerant entry, then read the units attached to the quantity. The material names span their associated engine rows, so an otherwise unlabeled continuation row still belongs to the material above it. Oil and refrigerant have separate quantities and units. The capacity table alone does not establish how much oil to add after a particular component repair.

Use the engine qualifier beside the range and the unit shown at the top of this table. The thermostat-like temptation to call any visible gap 'close enough' has no place here: this is a specified clearance. A comparison needs the matching measurement procedure; this table supplies the applicable range without establishing measurement points, setup or adjustment steps.
